== Biography ==
Agnes was born in 1795. She is the daughter of [[Glasgow-1466|Peter Glasgow]] and [[Dick-6841|Elizabeth Dick]].
== Research Notes ==
=== Father identity scope reviewed, 26 October 2026 ===

The complete selected father-profile proposition is now assessed at 82% (probable), superseding the 98% review retained below. Agnes’s 1795 Bathgate transcript names Peter Glasgow and Elisabeth Dick, matching the specific adult household and its 1783–1795 child sequence. It does not identify that adult as the Peter baptised at West Calder in 1762. Peter’s captured account expressly relies on neighbouring parishes, a compatible generation and repeated family names for that transition. For the complete selected father-profile proposition, retain a probable 82% rather than the previous 98%, which supported the named Bathgate father role. This reconciles scope with Andrew’s existing assessment, rather than treating shared derivative indexes as independent proof.

Provider transcripts and held family accounts reviewed; no parish original newly inspected. The Bathgate father role remains strongly supported. The 3-versus-5 March 1795 birth reading is a separate unresolved issue and is not the reason for this reduction. Maternity, Peter’s own father assessment and every family attachment remain unchanged.

=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1466]] is assessed at 98% (proved). The held Bathgate index and inspected provider transcript name Peter Glasgow and Elisabeth Dick for Agnes in 1795, baptized22 March. The3 March profile birthday versus5 March transcript is a reading conflict within the same identified family, not evidence for another father.

=== Current research ===

The Bathgate entry names Peter Glasgow and Elisabeth Dick and explicitly reports birth 5 March and baptism 22 March 1795, OPR 662/2 item 1. The current profile/catalogue birthday is 3 March 1795. The parents and event identify the existing child, but the 3-versus-5 March reading is unresolved without comparing the underlying source. The profile retains both readings visible and do not silently overwrite the birthday or create a second child.
